questions.prompt: Why does `streamText` keep the last line of each batch in `buffer` instead of parsing it straight away?
options: The provider sends the last line twice
Keeping it makes the model write faster
A network batch can end in the middle of a line, and parsing half a line of JSON would fail
questions.explanation: Bytes arrive in batches that ignore line endings. The last line may be cut off, so it waits in the buffer until the next batch completes it.

questions.prompt: Three deltas arrive with content "The capital", " is" and " Paris.". What should your program show?
options: "The capital is Paris.", the deltas joined in order
"The capitalThe capital is", each delta repeating the earlier ones
questions.explanation: Each delta holds only the new text since the last piece. Joining them in order gives the full reply.

questions.prompt: A reply takes 6 seconds to generate. What does streaming change?
options: The first words appear after a fraction of a second, though the full reply still takes about 6 seconds
The full reply now takes about 1 second
The model sees the context window in pieces
questions.explanation: Streaming does not speed up the model. It shortens the wait before something appears, because each piece is sent as soon as it is written.
